insight.title: Why One Small Interaction Sets the Tone for Your Day
insight.subtitle: How your brain uses early cues to decide how you will feel later.

sections.text: Have you noticed how one sharp comment can color an entire afternoon? In nature, a single crystal seed dictates the shape of a massive mineral. Your brain uses tiny initial cues the same way.
This is affective priming. Your mind takes the first small emotion it encounters and uses it as a template. One minor interaction doesn’t just pass; it creates a lens for everything that follows.
We often try to fix big problems at the end, but momentum starts at the beginning. A tiny adjustment in your first few seconds can prevent a massive, unwanted crystallization of stress later.
Try this today: The next time you start a conversation today, begin with a small note of appreciation.
You don't need to move the mountain; you only need to choose where the first pebble falls.
